m.d: The symbol for the number zero, that is "0."
m.e: The new job added a zero to my pay, from $20,000 to $200,000.

m.d: A person or thing that is worth nothing.
m.e: I'm not inviting him, he's total zero.

m.d: To zero is to make a small change to reset a piece of equipment.
m.e: I had to zero the counter on my tape player.

m.d: To zero in is to make small changes that bring you closer to something.
m.e: I was able to zero in on the source of bad smell in the shed.

m.d: Zero is a count of nothing, the number before one. It is often written 0.
Zero is also used with an uncountable noun.
Zealand is the largest island of Denmark.
Zealand is a province in the Southwestern of the Netherlands.
m.e: There are many sights in Zealand.

m.d: Zealand is a shortening of New Zealand.
An animal that somewhat looks like a horse, but has black and white stripes.
m.e: We saw zebras while we were in Africa.

m.d: By extension, any black and white stripe pattern that looks like a zebra.
m.e: I want to paint the room with zebra stripes.

m.d: If someone has zeal, they work very hard at a certain goal.
m.e: My brother is training with great zeal – he practices at every spare moment so that he can make the soccer team.

m.d: If you have zest, you are full of excitement or enthusiasm; you are full of life.
If food has zest, it has a lot of flavor. It might be spicy.
m.e: The hot peppers add zest to the soup.

m.d: If music has zest, it is fast and lively.
m.e: Play it with more zest this time.

m.d: If you zest something, you take the zest off of the fruit.
